1:1.t: Obadiah prophesies against Edom, the nation descended from Esau, Jacob's brother, for its treachery when Jerusalem fell in 586 BC. Compare Jeremiah 49:7-22 and Psalm 137:7.

1:3.t: "The clefts of the rocks": Edom's capital, Sela (later Petra), was carved into high rock cliffs. Sela means "rock".

1:7.t: "But you will not detect it": the KJV's "there is none understanding in him".

1:19.t: "The Negev ... the foothills": the KJV's "the south ... the plain".

1:20.t: Sepharad: an unknown place, perhaps Sardis in Asia Minor. "The Negev": the KJV's "the south".

1:21.t: "And the kingdom will be the LORD's": the book ends with God's rule over all nations, the hope of every prophet. Compare Revelation 11:15.
